title: Subscription smoothing & proactive surprise-billing protections PRD
creator: Ava Patel
description: High-level feature PRD for subscription smoothing, soft-throttles, proactive notices, and automatic emergency crediting to minimize customer surprise bills and improve retention for high-variance workloads.
context: Multiple customers with bursty workloads reported unexpected bills after seasonal or campaign-driven spikes. Current behavior: hard overage charges post-invoice with limited proactive signals. This PRD defines a suite of product and billing controls to smooth consumption, give customers transparent previews, and provide automatic protections for customers at risk of bill shock.
goals: Reduce customer-initiated disputes for overage charges by 60% within 3 months of launch
Provide an invoice preview and actionable warnings at 70%, 85%, and 95% of committed entitlements
Introduce a soft-throttle mode that gracefully degrades throughput for non-critical routes instead of immediate hard rejection
Implement a per-customer emergency credit flow that can automatically cap charges when threshold breached
Make smoothing policies opt-in and visible in Console with clear accounting for audit and billing teams
non_goals: We will not overhaul base pricing or per-token unit prices in this scope
We will not implement predictive billing model that guarantees precise future spend forecasts (future phase)
We will not change auditing export formats for legal requests in this iteration
product_requirements: Subscription Smoothing: allow merchants to configure a smoothing window (default 7 days) where overage beyond committed quota is absorbed from a refundable smoothing buffer before invoiceable overage is recorded
Soft-Throttle Modes: per-route and per-caller throttle profiles (grace, degraded, reject) with default fallback to 'grace' for customer-configured non-critical routes
Proactive Notices: system-generated warnings at configurable thresholds (70%, 85%, 95%) delivered via Console, email, and webhook with recommended mitigation actions
Invoice Preview API: provide /billing/preview endpoint returning projected invoice and line-itemized overage under current smoothing and throttle settings
Emergency Credit Policy: auto-apply short-term escrow credit up to configurable dollar cap when projected overage > X% of committed plan and customer has negative reaction signal enabled
Audit Trail: every smoothing/credit decision must have immutable audit record with triggering event, policy applied, and contact who approved auto-credit (system or ops)
Opt-in/Opt-out: default behavior for existing customers remains unchanged; smoothing and auto-credit must be opt-in with opt-out available in Console
Metrics & Billing Reconciliation: smoothing buffer consumption must be mapped to ledger entries and exposed to billing reconciliation system for month-end settlement
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: When smoothing is enabled and a customer exceeds committed quota by up to buffer amount, the invoice at month end must reflect 0 overage charge and a smoothing ledger entry describing buffer consumption
AC-2: Invoice Preview API returns consistent numbers with final invoice when smoothing and throttle policies are applied in simulated replay within 1% deviation for tokenized workloads
AC-3: Console triggers proactive warnings at configured thresholds within 5 minutes of threshold crossing and links to mitigation docs

AC-4: Soft-Throttle applied to a non-critical route must reduce allowed concurrency/throughput and return structured response codes (429 with body "grace-throttled" or 200 with degraded quality) per spec

AC-5: Emergency auto-credit is applied automatically only if customer has opt-in flag and projected overage exceeds emergency threshold; credit application generates ledger record and customer notification within 10 minutes
AC-6: Billing reconciliation team can export smoothing buffer usage as CSV and totals match ledger within tolerance of 0.5%
AC-7: Unit and integration test coverage implemented for invoice preview, smoothing ledgers, and throttle state machine with >= 85% code coverage across the billing module
edge_cases_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: making smoothing default could increase bad-faith usage; chosen approach: opt-in default to balance protection vs abuse
Edge-case: customers who aggressively use smoothing across multiple tenants; mitigate via per-account caps and anomaly detection labels
Tradeoff: soft-throttle latency vs quality — we will favor immediate availability with degraded quality for non-critical routes to maintain responsiveness
Edge-case: retroactive disputes if smoothing buffer was applied incorrectly; require immutable audit and automated rollback path with ops approval
Tradeoff: complexity of ledger mapping — keep smoothing as a separate ledger bucket to simplify month-end reconciliation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): enable smoothing and invoice-preview for Redwood internal accounts and a pilot of up to 10 customers. Phase 2 (private beta): open to invited customers with billing & legal sign-off and Console UI toggles. Phase 3 (general availability): default opt-in UI for new customers and billing API documentation. Each phase requires billing reconciliation sign-off and a canary of 48 hours with real traffic checks.
monitoring_and_metrics: Metric: Number of proactive notices sent and click-through rate to mitigation docs
Metric: Emergency credits auto-applied count and total dollar value
Metric: Throttle-induced error rate on non-critical routes
customer_communication: Draft email and Console banner templates will be prepared: (1) Invitation to pilot with clear opt-in instructions, (2) Real-time warning templates at 70/85/95% thresholds, (3) Post-month invoice explainer highlighting smoothing usage and any emergency credits applied.
security_and_compliance_considerations: No new secrets created. Audit trail must be retained per existing billing retention policy (7 years). Any auto-credit operations must go through RBAC-guarded service account and be logged for SOC review.
dependencies: ENG-28211: Billing ledger export enhancements (needed for reconciliation)
ENG-29340: Console UI toggles and notifications framework
ENG-30012: Throttle state machine and per-route QoS flags
ENG-31001: Invoice-preview API and simulation replay infra
PM-120000: Legal review for emergency credit policy
open_questions: What is the default smoothing buffer size for new customers (suggested default: 7 days / $1000 cap)?
Should emergency credits be refundable to Redwood or recorded as deferred revenue adjustments?
What signals should count as 'non-critical route' by default? Product wants SDK routes and embeddings marked; engineering owns final mapping
What SLA do we promise for Invoice Preview API response latency under production load (target < 1s median)?
implementation_notes: Engineering to provide a migration path for accounts that have custom billing pipelines. Billing ops will run a dry-reconciliation pass for the pilot month to validate smoothing ledger mappings. Provide a feature flag 'smoothing.enable' gated by customer ID for early rollout.
